tier_reason: The README Performance table gives first-party console.time numbers (uWrap 82/90/185 ms vs canvas-hypertxt 770/1660/1430 ms in Chrome 135, Firefox 137, Safari 18.1). The harness is public (demo/index.html with a vendored demo/canvas-hypertxt.mjs and demo/txtgen.mjs), but there is no machine or CPU model, only one console.time run per library and no independent measurement, so it stays at C.

corrections.workload: 100,000 random sentences (demo/txtgen.mjs) wrapped at random widths of 50-250px, using a Canvas2D context set to 14px Inter with letterSpacing 0.15px. uWrap is timed as varPreLine(ctx) setup plus count(text, width) per sentence. canvas-hypertxt is timed as split(ctx, text, font, width, true) per sentence, with hyper-wrapping enabled, and the length of the returned array is read. Each library is timed once with console.time on the demo page (demo/index.html), run from the DevTools console.
corrections.caveats: The baseline is a third-party canvas wrapping helper (glideapps/canvas-hypertxt, 138 stars, used by Glide Data Grid), not HarfBuzz or FreeType. This is Latin-only line wrapping at the edge of the shaping and layout category, so the entry is off-baseline. The harness does not time the same calls. uWrap is timed through count(), which only increments a counter and allocates no line strings. canvas-hypertxt is timed through split(), which slices and trims an array of line strings and builds a string cache key for every call. uWrap's split() was not benchmarked, so part of the gap comes from the different work. Each library draws its own random widths, so the two do not wrap identical (text, width) pairs. Each figure is a single console.time run with no repetitions or warm-up control, and uWrap always runs first. Browsers are named but the machine and CPU are not. Both libraries approximate wrapping instead of measuring every line. uWrap sums per-character widths from a one-time lookup table plus uppercase-pair kerning, works for Latin text and the pre-line strategy only, and does not handle \r\n. canvas-hypertxt in hyper mode switches to a trained per-character estimate (times 1.01) after about 500k characters. The README's accuracy and memory claims have no numbers: accuracy is shown only as visual overlays on the demo page.

notes: The numbers match the README exactly: 9.4x (Chrome), 18.4x (Firefox) and 7.7x (Safari), derived from page data. The main shortcoming is that the harness times uWrap count() against canvas-hypertxt split(), which allocates line strings. The last commit is 2025-08-01 (14 months old, so stale), the license is MIT, there are 319 stars, and it is not a fork. The only issue (#1) is a word-break TODO, and no independent measurement was found.
